solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Choral work about Knight's farewell

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
N is the chess notation for a knight; the 's reads as 'has'
ta-ta is a casual goodbye

explanation.surface: A choir sings a piece about a knight saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung composition for voices and instruments, often sacred, so it is a choral work.

clue.text: Friend in Roman Catholic church first to get hard material

indicators.note: first places the church before the rest

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: in places the friend inside the Catholic letters

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A friend in a Catholic church gets the first chance at some tough material.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic is a hard, brittle substance made by firing clay, such as porcelain.

clue.text: Rover's escalating curse about love

definitions.note: rover is, with 's as 'is'; a rover is a wanderer

indicators.note: the curse goes around the zero
in a down clue escalating means going up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: damn is a curse
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A rover's swearing gets steadily worse over a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a person who roams from place to place with no fixed home, a wanderer.

clue.text: Store that offers a service

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic Eucharistic service

explanation.surface: A shop that also holds church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' looks like a noun, a shop, but is the verb meaning gather up.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect and accumulate a quantity, a synonym of store up.

clue.text: Study in summer, that's said to provide supplementary material

indicators.note: that's said tells us the built word is spoken, and what is heard is the entry

parts.note: a den (study) goes inside an adder (summer, one who sums), giving ADD-DEN-ER

explanation.surface: Someone studies in summer, which apparently supplies extra material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who adds up; ADDENDER spoken in a non-rhotic accent gives the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the end of a book or document, extra supporting matter.

clue.text: Stabilising material delivery to a street

parts.note: in cricket a ball is one delivery from the bowler

explanation.surface: A load of stabilising material is delivered to a street address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a parcel, but in cricket it is one ball bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is heavy material such as gravel or water carried low in a ship to keep it steady.

clue.text: Dickens work translated by graduate with no time to adopt 'new British' in parts

indicators.note: translated means the letters are turned into a different form, a rearrangement
T for time is taken away from the word graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate in a hurry translates a Dickens novel, working new British material into its parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no time' removes T from GRADUATE; 'to adopt' brings N and BR into the pool, and 'translated' rearranges BY, GRADUAE, N and BR.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is Charles Dickens's 1841 novel set around the Gordon Riots, one of his works.

clue.text: City's municipal officer left day room refurbished by the end of October

indicators.note: a refurbished room is rearranged, so its letters are mixed
the end of takes the final letter of October

explanation.surface: A city official leaves the day room redecorated by late October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City's' refers to the City of London, whose head is the Lord Mayor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Mayor is the ceremonial elected head of the City of London and certain other cities.

clue.text: Group of stars with capital deserted America

parts.note: and means together with
Rome is the Italian capital
D is the abbreviation for deserted, as in military records

explanation.surface: A star cluster is linked to a capital city that has abandoned America.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a northern constellation, a named pattern of stars, also home to a nearby galaxy.

clue.text: Journeyed long and hard with two kings usurping son in Gobi rising?

indicators.note: to usurp is to take another's place, so the kings replace the son
in a down clue rising means read upwards

parts.note: the Gobi is a desert, so it stands for that word, as the question mark hints
K is the chess abbreviation for king, twice

explanation.surface: Two kings overthrow a son out in the Gobi and set off on an arduous march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns DESERT into TRESED; the S is then swapped for KK.
explanation.definitionFit: To trek is to make a long, arduous journey, usually on foot.

clue.text: Strike horseman capturing a thief with vehicle?

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard

indicators.note: the horseman captures, i.e. holds within him, the letter a

parts.note: a rider is someone on horseback

explanation.surface: A rider on strike seizes a thief who has a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A ram-raider is a British term for a thief who drives a vehicle through a shop front to loot it; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ram-raiding is theft carried out by smashing a car or van into premises, so the culprit is a thief using a vehicle.

clue.text: See 5 down
Princess embraced by secret society member becoming President

indicators.note: the princess is held inside the society member

parts.note: a Freemason, or Mason, belongs to a famously secretive society
Di, as in Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A princess is welcomed by a Freemason who goes on to become President.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States.

clue.text: A jolly grapple in wrestling

parts.note: a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM
a lock is a hold that pins an opponent's limb in wrestling

explanation.surface: Two wrestlers enjoy a cheerful bit of grappling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is the crossword term for a Royal Marine; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlock is a wrestling hold that immobilises an opponent's arm, exactly such a grapple.

clue.text: Bird that's scary was wild about nothing

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the zero
wild says the letters run free into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A frightening bird ran amok over nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large flightless bird of New Guinea and northern Australia.

clue.text: Rascal unscrambled clues on empty road

indicators.note: unscrambled tells us to sort the letters into a new order
an empty road keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A rogue works out the cryptic clues on a deserted road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves RD from road, which joins CLUESON in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest or unprincipled person, a rogue or rascal.

clue.text: In difficulty there and then

definitions.meaning: in a tricky position, put under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both put in an awkward position and right away at the place itself.

clue.text: Surrender yard for furlong in open country

indicators.note: one unit is put in place of the other, the yard standing for the furlong

parts.note: a field is open land
F is the abbreviation for furlong

explanation.surface: Giving up a yard in place of a furlong in open countryside sounds like a racecourse compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or give up, a direct synonym of surrender as a verb.

clue.text: Tobacco tin no longer in fashion

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
something out is no longer stylish

explanation.surface: A tobacco tin has gone out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tobacco tin' reads as one object, but the tin is chemical symbol SN.
explanation.definitionFit: Snout is British slang, especially prison slang, for tobacco or a cigarette.

clue.text: Makes fun of cat climbing to eat what's left?

indicators.note: the cat eats, taking the leftovers inside it
in a down clue climbing means read upwards

parts.note: puss is a cat
an end is a remnant, as in a cigarette end

explanation.surface: A cat climbs up to finish off the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to parody or mock, a British idiom for making fun of someone.

clue.text: Significant part in MOT is damaged

indicators.note: a damaged part is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car fails its MOT because a vital component is damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Important and significant are synonyms, both meaning of real consequence.

clue.text: Pays no attention to Italian ladies, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: signore is the Italian plural of signora, a lady

explanation.surface: Someone snubs Italian women, sending the first to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to disregard it or take no notice of it.

clue.text: Gas for audible suffering

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: audible means we take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: pain is suffering

explanation.surface: A gas used to treat suffering you can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used as bottled fuel.

clue.text: Current destroyed coal pit

indicators.note: a destroyed pit is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A present-day coal mine has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity near a coal pit; it means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means relating to present events, the matters of the moment.

clue.text: Gran eager to get cloth

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Grandma is keen to get hold of some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally from Nanjing, a type of cloth.

clue.text: Type of vehicle with clear roof

parts.note: open as in clear or unobstructed
the top of a vehicle is its roof

explanation.surface: A kind of car with a transparent roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-top bus or car has no roof, a recognised style of vehicle.

clue.text: Order English thesaurus (shortened version)

indicators.note: the reference book's name is cut down to its familiar short form

parts.note: a thesaurus is a kind of word reference, here a dictionary

explanation.surface: Instructions for an abridged English thesaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official proclamation or command, an order from authority.

clue.text: Common vegetable forming part of pasta terrine

indicators.note: forming part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ordinary vegetable goes into a pasta terrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater is informal slang for a potato, the commonest of vegetables.

clue.text: Old US money in pilgrim's pouch

definitions.meaning: provisional paper currency issued in the US in place of coin
an archaic word for a small bag or wallet carried by a traveller

explanation.surface: Antique American banknotes turn up in a pilgrim's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrip names both emergency paper money and the satchel once carried by pilgrims and beggars.

clue.text: Article is rewritten true to life

indicators.note: a rewritten piece has its letters put into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is revised to be more faithful to reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic describes art or writing that represents things accurately, as they really are.

clue.text: Exercise routine consisting of one carrying sheets of metal? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within
this reverses the roles, so the sheets hold the one rather than the one holding the sheets

parts.note: plates are flat sheets of metal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A workout regime that has someone hefting metal sheets, though the clue then flips it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, I would contain PLATES; 'Quite the opposite!' turns it so PLATES contains I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of controlled exercises for core strength, named after Joseph Pilates.

clue.text: Penetrate a length of intestine

parts.note: to enter is to go into, penetrate

explanation.surface: A probe goes into a stretch of gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral is a medical adjective meaning relating to or by way of the gut.
